_comment: The twelve accuracy checks, written down 2026-09-06 so a score can be RECOMPUTED.
They existed before as a sentence in README.md -- 'technical proper nouns, an invented
surname, four figures and a date, two spoken self-corrections, and one near-homophone
pair' -- which does not add up to twelve and cannot be re-run. Every N/12 in that table
was therefore unreproducible, which is what claude-skills-luwe was filed for.
The audio is NOT in this repository and must not be: it lives outside, and score.py takes
a path to a transcript. It is a scripted 2 min 19 s read by one speaker into a laptop
microphone, with a fictional company and an invented surname, so nothing here discloses
anything. Regenerate the transcripts with scripts/transcribe.py, then run score.py.
A check has `expect` (must match) and optionally `reject` (must not match). Both are
case-insensitive regexes over the transcript body. `reject` exists because several of
these fail by producing a PLAUSIBLE wrong string rather than by producing nothing --
'terror grunt' for Terragrunt, 'board packs up' for board pack -- and an expect-only
check scores those as a simple miss rather than as the confident error they are.

A check must measure whether the CONTENT survived, not whether it was formatted a particular way. The figure checks were digit-only until 2026-09-06 and scored a correct spelled-out transcription as a miss -- found by an independent fact-check of the README, not by the suite.

TWO KINDS OF CHECK, and confusing them is how the figure bug happened. For a PROPER NOUN the form IS the test: 'Terragrunt' spelled 'terror grunt' is the failure being measured, so a single spelling is correct and must not be widened. For a FIGURE, a DATE or a QUANTITY the form is incidental: 'forty-two thousand three hundred euros' and '42,300' are the same fact, and a pattern that accepts only one of them measures formatting instead of accuracy. Widen the second kind; never widen the first.

source.description: scripted meeting, one speaker, laptop built-in microphone, real room
source.sha256_note: hash the file you use and record it in the results, so a later run is comparable

checks.note: The single hardest token here. Fails as 'terror grunt', which reads as words.
Three letters, spoken. Confusable with AKS in the same sentence.
The pair matters: the sentence says EKS moves and AKS stays. Swapping them inverts it.
Two words, a product name, said once.
Said twice in one sentence, so a backend that drops one still passes.
Invented, so no backend has it memorised. The speaker even says it comes up wrong every time.
Fails as 'north wind', which is why it is the --replace example in the README.
18 units off the old root configuration. Spoken as 'eighteen'.

42,300 euros. MEASURED 2026-09-06: ElevenLabs rendered this as 'forty-two thousand three hundred euros' on one run and '€42,300' on the next, from the same audio. A digit-only pattern scored the first as a MISS for a figure that was transcribed perfectly, so the check was measuring whether a number had been digitised rather than whether it survived. Both forms count.
Against a forecast of 38,000. Spelled-out form accepted for the same reason as figure-budget -- most backends write this one in words.
Spoken as 'the fourteenth of November'. A date is the thing a reader acts on.
The speaker corrects himself about which cluster moves. Dropping the correction leaves a confident wrong statement.

99.95% versus 99.5% in the same breath. mlx-whisper large-v3 loses BOTH the figure and the word 'correction' that introduced it, rendering the sentence as '99.5%, not Not 99.5%' -- a correction that reads as if it were captured.
EVERY backend measured so far fails this one, producing 'board packs up'. Kept in the set precisely because it is the case no threshold catches: it is grammatical, fluent and wrong.
